name: Georgia
source: Georgia HB 463 as signed 2026-05-11 (https://gov.georgia.gov/document/2026-signed-legislation/hb-463/download, read 2026-10-24): flat 4.99% for taxable years from 2026-01-01, standard deduction 15,000 single and separate / 30,000 joint, dependent exemption 5,000, retirement exclusion 35,000 / 65,000 (70,000 from 2027); Georgia DOR Important Tax Updates (https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates, read 2026-10-24) agrees on the rate and deduction; 2025 IT-511 booklet for the base, exemptions and Social Security

state_base.note: Georgia starts from federal adjusted gross income (2025 IT-511 booklet, Form 500 line 8, read 2026-10-24) and conforms to the IRC as of 2025-01-01, so 401(k)/403(b) deferrals, Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits keep their federal treatment (no add-back is listed). Not modelled: the HB 463 exclusion of up to 1,750 each of overtime and tips from 2026 (Georgia did not adopt the federal deductions).

income_brackets.note: Flat 4.99% for taxable years from 2026-01-01 (HB 463 as signed 2026-05-11; the DOR Important Tax Updates page agrees), read 2026-10-24. The revenue-triggered cuts from 2027 are not modelled.

standard_deduction.note: HB 463, tax years from 2026: 15,000 single, head of household and separate, 30,000 joint (enacted text and Georgia DOR Important Tax Updates, read 2026-10-24; 12,000 / 24,000 in 2025). The act raises them by 375 / 750 a year from 2027 up to 18,000 / 36,000, subject to revenue-trigger delays. Not modelled: the tips and overtime exclusions.

exemptions.note: No personal exemptions and no additional deduction for 65 or older or blind (the 2025 IT-511 standard deduction table lists none, read 2026-10-24), so senior is 0; dependent is 5,000 from 2026 (HB 463, up from 4,000; it rises 125 a year from 2027 to 6,000, subject to the same delays).

retirement_exclusion.note: Retirement income exclusion (O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(5); HB 463 enacted text and 2025 IT-511 booklet, read 2026-10-24): per person, 35,000 at 62-64 (or permanently disabled) and 65,000 at 65 or older through 2026, 70,000 at 65 or older from 2027; each spouse qualifies separately. Approximated with one tier: 65,000 from 65; ages 62-64 get no exclusion here. Georgia's exclusion also covers interest, dividends, capital gains, rent and up to 5,000 of earned income; the model applies it to retirement distributions only.

estate_inheritance.note: Georgia has no estate tax and no inheritance tax (Tax Foundation 2026 estate and inheritance tax map, https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/estate-inheritance-taxes/, and state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax agree). Confirmed primary on https://dor.georgia.gov/estate-tax-faq (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

social_security.note: Georgia subtracts Social Security and Railroad Retirement included in federal AGI (2025 IT-511 booklet, Schedule 1 subtraction 5, read 2026-10-24), so benefits are exempt. Kiplinger 2026 and state-costs.csv column ss_taxed agree.

local_income_tax.check_at: Tax Foundation local income taxes primer
local_income_tax.note: Georgia cities and counties levy no income tax (Tax Foundation local income tax list and state-costs.csv local_income_tax agree).

sales_tax.check_at: Georgia revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: 0.07 from the state's own source (Georgia title ad valorem tax 7.0% of the fair market value, one-time, in place of sales tax (https://dor.georgia.gov/motor-vehicles/vehicle-registration-license-plates/vehicle-taxes-title-ad-valorem-tax-tavt-and, validation run 2)). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: yes); research note: State 4% exempt for food; LOST/SPLOST/ESPLOST/MARTA etc. apply (e.g. 2% Cherokee); HOST/FLOST portions may exempt. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Some towns tax groceries and others do not; the estimate uses the general average local rate, so it overstates. Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.source: Georgia annual passenger-car registration of 20 (fee guides found in the s292 search, 2026-10-22) and state-costs.csv column vehicle_tax
car_taxes.note: Annual registration of about 20; vehicles bought since 2013 pay the one-time 7% title ad valorem tax (TAVT, in sales_tax.vehicle_rate) instead of a yearly ad valorem tax. Weak sources, so unconfirmed. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py; average_annual set by hand in s292 (rerunning the importer resets it to 0). Confirmed primary on https://dor.georgia.gov/motor-vehicles/vehicle-registration-license-plates/motor-vehicles-fees-fines-and-penalties (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

fuel.source: Excise: https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/motor-fuel-tax/calculating-tax-motor-fuel (validation run 2, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel: 0.333 ($0.333/gal, 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31); average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Georgia insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
